items.name: Kafka partitions and committed offsets
items.explanation: Kafka splits a topic into partitions that keep their order. A consumer records how far it has read, its committed offset, and resumes from there after a restart.

assumedBy.quote: However, this would cause potential data loss. For example, if a consumer is restarted, it will resume from largest committed offsets;

items.name: gRPC
items.explanation: gRPC is a way for one service to call another over the network. The call and its reply are described in a shared definition, and each message is sent separately.

assumedBy.quote: Sends/pushes each message separately to a consumer service instance

items.name: Google Cloud Pub/Sub
items.explanation: A managed publish and subscribe service from Google Cloud. Spotify's system sits on it instead of running its own brokers.

assumedBy.quote: It took us almost a year to design, write, deploy and scale the current, Cloud Pub/Sub-based Event Delivery system fully into production.

items.name: ETL
items.explanation: Extract, transform and load: copy data out of the systems that produce it, clean it up, and load it into one store where it can be analysed.

assumedBy.quote: You can read more about this concept in Reliable export of Cloud Pub/Sub streams to Cloud Storage, a blog post explaining all technicalities of our ETL.

items.name: Service level agreements
items.explanation: An SLA is an agreed promise about how a service will perform, such as delivering on time and at a stated quality. Spotify ranks its events by whether one is attached.

assumedBy.quote: These Event Types are subject to external SLAs both for timely delivery, and quality

sources.title: Service Level Objectives (Site Reliability Engineering, chapter 4)
